newsitem.title: UK: EMERGING MARKET OUTLOOK - IMF, U.S. set tone.
newsitem.headline: EMERGING MARKET OUTLOOK - IMF, U.S. set tone.

text.p: Year-end profit taking on any market upswings and International Monetary Fund (IMF) activity in Eastern Europe will set much of the tone for emerging market investors this week.

Uncertainty about U.S. markets before Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the Fed body charged with setting interest rate policy, will also keep investors very wary about potential surprises.

After a spotted performance last week when emerging markets partly followed a spooked U.S. market lower, investors are looking for a quiet week marked largely by consolidation and some year-end profit taking.
RUSSIA was the subject of considerable activity over the weekend, with the IMF deciding late on Friday to resume lending there under its $10 billion programme.
The IMF had delayed some tranches until it was more certain the government was doing its bit to increase revenues.
And on Sunday, Russian parliament passed the 1997 draft budget in the first reading.
The decision is expected to give a lift to Russian debt and equity prices though traders said activity was likely to stay fairly slow as the holiday period approached.
The IMF has also just given its backing to ROMANIA, which IMF Managing Director Michael Camdessus is due to visit on Friday.

The IMF suspended a three-year standby credit of $460 million this year after criticising the policies of the leftist government thrown out in last month's general election, but a senior IMF official praised the new government last week and said it was committed to reforms.
"There is an optimistic bend to Romania," said David Mars, director of emerging Europe economics research at SBC Warburg, particularly if the new government dismantled its foreign exchange regime.
POLAND, where the bourse rose nearly three percent late last week, will release November consumer and producer prices on Monday. Investors are expecting it show continuing signs of deterioration.
"The market has given up on further progress on inflation," Mars said.
Further south, TURKEY'S markets will be haunted by the downgrading of its long-term foreign currency debt late on Friday by rating agency Standard & Poor's to single-B from B-plus.
Turkish stocks immediately opened lower on Monday on the rating news.

Fixed income investors will closely follow the five-day parliament debate in GREECE on the 1997 budget beginning on Tuesday. One analyst said the deep social unrest in Greece demonstrated the government's commitment to fiscal reform.
"The demonstrations are positive signs that the ordinary Greeks think the government is very serious," Mars said.
Renewed sales of Iraqi oil under the United Nations' oil-for-food agreement will continue to buoy JORDAN on anticipation of Iraqi demand for excess Jordanian industrial capacity.
"There may be some profit-taking, but the trend will remain strong," said Basir Siman, director of North African and Middle East equity research at Union Bank of Switzerland in London.
Investors in EGYPT will adopt a wait and see attitude with potential for some profit-taking, he said.
Meanwhile, Latin American markets were expected to be quiet in the run-up to Christmas, but further drops in the U.S. bond market could particularly affect MEXICO and ARGENTINA.
ARGENTINA releases November unemployment data on Wednesday which is expected to hold steady around 17 percent.
"It might be a negative there compounding worries, but generally things are getting better," said Alan Livsey, head of Latin American research at Kleinwort Benson.
Equity markets in CHILE could be boosted by speculation of a rate cut in the new year.

Investors in BRAZIL will monitor pre-campaign activities in the re-election attempt by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, who will need a rewriting of the constitution in order to stand for a second term.
The IFC emerging market composite investable index, IFC/IPRD, denominated in dollars was down 1.8 percent week on week at 295.94 points on Friday.
Latin America was down 2.8 percent, Asia was 0.6 lower and Europe, Middle East and Africa fell 3.1 percent.
